annotations.text:
What changed on this page — now shipped in DetourReports.tsx (v1.5.108)

1. Status is a tab bar with live counts, and ACTIVE is the default — no more "all statuses" plus a separate Show/Hide history toggle deciding the same thing twice. Each count reflects what the other filters already allow.
2. Search is promoted to a full-width field; the other five filters moved behind a Filters button with a count badge, and every applied filter shows as a removable chip. Clearing the filters keeps the status tab.
3. Fifteen columns became seven plus a disclosure control. Avail number, path, workflow, reason, severity, source and provenance moved into the expanded record — the CSV export still carries all 51 fields.
4. The expanded record is a labelled definition grid instead of a stack of dim sentences.
5. Rows disclose through a real button with aria-expanded, so the record is keyboard-reachable for the first time.

The detour data on these artboards is invented sample content — plausible MVTA corridors, not real records.

Export, added after this canvas was drawn

The Export button now opens a preview before anything downloads: the file name, the row and column counts, the filters it was taken under, and the rows themselves. From there, Download CSV or Open in browser — the same export rendered as a standalone HTML page in a new tab.

The preview and the file are generated from one table (detourExportTable), so they cannot drift apart. See the shipped page rather than these artboards for that dialog.

Legacy spreadsheet history: removed

The whole subcard is gone — the imported-rows table, the Show/Hide toggle, and the CSV/JSON upload control that lived inside it.

Worth knowing: that upload was the ONLY way to import retired-tracker rows. Removing the panel removes the import path from the console. The rows and POST /detours/historical-imports stay; nothing is deleted.
